newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate up on pre-FOMC woes.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate up on pre-FOMC woes.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were up 150 basis points from a low prior close to 18.50 percent in early trade on Monday due to speculative pressure ahead of Tuesday's U.S. Federal Open Market Committee talks, dealers said.
"The market is under pressure from light speculation due to concerns over domestic data, like GDP, and external events like the FOMC meeting," a trader said.
First quarter GDP data were expected from the Finance Ministry at an unspecified time on Monday.
Dealers said predictions were mixed over whether the FOMC would raise U.S. interest rates.
"We are waiting for the FOMC decision tomorrow and...the event could exert pressure if they increase base rates," one dealer said.
Dealers said strong first quarter GDP data would be well received by the market as a sign of recovery from a severe recession in 1995.

"As long as GDP (growth) is close to 5.0 percent it will have been laregly discounted by the market. But if it is greater, then we could see capital inflow that would lower primary and secondary rates," a trader said.
Overnight rates on bank paper matched the upward trend on government rates and increased 30 basis points to 19.50 percent in early trade.
Liquidity of 255 million pesos was due to return to the system from prior central bank participation.
